## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Bāshī jīng* (T581) is a one-fascicle short sūtra translated by Zhī Qiān 支謙 ([支謙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E8%AC%99)) at the Wú 吳 court. The Buddha enumerates "eight teachers" (*bāshī* 八師) — eight aspects of the human condition (killing, theft, sexual misconduct, lying, drunkenness, old age, sickness, death) that have instructed him on the way to liberation.

**Abstract**

A short didactic sūtra typical of Zhī Qiān's *Āgama*-derived corpus, datable to his Wú-period activity (222–252 CE) at Wǔchāng 武昌 and Jiànyè 建業. The "eight teachers" device — calamities re-read as masters — became a popular Buddhist trope in Six-Dynasties literature.
